title: Im a 3D artist with no coding skills. Any AI tools help me to make a game?
author: NonSatanicGoat
selftext: I'm an artist but my coding knowledge is slightly higher than a chimp. Is there any tools that can help me code my game? Unity or Unreal; paid or free it doesnt matter.

comments.author: GamingWithMyDog
comments.body: I was the same way. Visual scripting combined with tutorials got me really far. Playmaker for Unity was the standard 10 years ago but it’s probably changed

comments.author: Wooden-Hovercraft688
comments.body:
You can get a game template for what you want. A lot of indie games do it, just don't talk about it. 


You won't learn everything this way, but it may give you the incentive to keep going, doing the tweekings you need, adding mechanics


To me it was easier to learn this way. I felt less overwhelmed then expand from there until you learn to do it from zero


Since I'm not a 3d artist, unreal have way more free assets and quixel, thats why I chose it. 


I use Gemini pro too, not exactly vibe coding, but sometimes you know what you want to do, but you lack the syntax and experience, you don't get the full code, you work from it. 


For other people, they say watching a ton of YouTube videos is better. Doing small copies, like making your own flap bird first.

replies.author: AncientAdamo
replies.body:
I can second Gemini...

For me it's been getting insanely good recently, even with more complex tasks

replies.author: pablo603
replies.body:
I third Gemini.

It handled a 5000 line script flawlessly. Not game dev related, it was javscript and I was fiddling around with npm, but still very impressive.

replies.author: pablo603
replies.body:
API via AI Studio. You get 100 requests per day for free for Gemini 2.5 pro which is quite a bit.

Can also use it without an API, there the limits are much higher for free.

replies.author: Wooden-Hovercraft688
replies.body:
Yeah, it must be the pro. 
Flash is horrible

comments.author: PigeonMaster2000
comments.body: [Nimble Fox](https://nimblefox.ai/) has not fully launched yet but you might be interested in checking it out

comments.author: Emergency_Mastodon56
comments.body: Claude AI is surprisingly good at walking you through the code, too. But I think you’ll find that you’re going to want to take courses or tutorials in the code of whatever engine you choose. The ai can be wrong, and of you don’t know enough to identify WHERE it went wrong, you’ll spend more time debugging than building.

replies.author: HelfenMich
replies.body: I can second that sentiment. I recently started in on gamedev but I'm already a dev of 15+ years. Most of my time is spent debugging AI code. No matter how well you document, sometimes it's just going to make incorrect assumptions. Or you update something and the AI doesn't fully understand the dependencies to update it everywhere it needs to be updated.

comments.author: spacespacespapce
comments.body: I have the exact opposite problem as you haha I can code but it's hard to create assets for me

comments.author: ioaia
comments.body: Augment Code is a great tool. It's a bit more expensive but it truly understand your codebase even very large.

comments.author: Whatsinthebox84
comments.body: Can you just do art on my website instead?

comments.author: Early_Situation_6552
comments.body:
are you trying to code? or are you trying to find your place?

if you're trying to find your place, you should either 1) market yourself as someone who does touch-ups of AI-generated placeholders assets that other developers bring you, to make them more professional and cohesive, or, 2) learn AI art generation pipeline frameworks (like ComfyUI) so that you can market yourself as an "AI-augmented" artist who can quickly generate very niche and high quality assets

replies.author: krullulon
replies.body: OP stated pretty clearly that they want to make their own game.

comments.body: Try out the site we are building, makko ai. Its all free right now while we are in beta.
